title: Prod launch checks and authorization escape hatch
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic pre-release security checklist plus an operational escape-hatch for short lead-time exceptions. It focuses on three things we keep tripping over in Dedicated and Private launches: RBAC v2 role drift, missing audit fields in token-level logs, and gaps in SIEM export/evidence automation so on-call can assemble a compliance bundle quickly.

Scope and intended audience:
- Scope: service releases touching inference control plane, auth, data-handling, and deployment orchestration. Includes Hosted API release pipelines when tenant-affecting.
- Audience: release engineer, SRE on-call, product security reviewer, controller/ops reviewer, release manager.

Quick checklist (pre-launch, minimum pass criteria):
1) RBAC v2 gate: role mapping verified and smoke-tested
   - Confirm all new API endpoints have roles in RBAC matrix and no permissive wildcards.
   - Verify role inheritance changes are documented in the RBAC change PR.
   - Run ad-hoc token with each role to a dev dogfood tenant; assert expected 200/403 behavior.
   - Evidence: recorded curl output or Playwright run, link to PR.

2) Audit log schema validation: required fields present
   - Required fields: timestamp_utc, request_id, actor_id, actor_role, resource_type, resource_id, action, result_status, client_ip, proxy_chain, kv_cache_hit (if applicable), seq_len_hint, model_variant_tag.
   - Ensure request_id is GUID and cross-wires with trace id.
   - Automate: run local schema validator against sample traffic capture.
   - Evidence: schema-validator run output + sample log snippet.

3) SIEM export mapping and retention check
   - Confirm export pipeline maps our audit fields into SIEM fields and retains raw event for minimum retention window.
   - Validate ingest via small test payload using staging SIEM sink.
   - Check alert rules: auth-failure spike, high-rate anonymous tokens, suspicious role escalation.

4) Evidence automation run: produce release bundle in <10 minutes
   - Run evidence-collector script (ops/evidence/collect-release-bundle). Expected outputs: RBAC diff, audit snippets, SIEM ingestion receipts, PR/commit list, canary metrics.
   - Record time-to-assemble; if >10m, note root cause.

5) Sign-off checklist (release manager + security)
   - Release manager confirms 1-4 complete. Security reviewer signs off if no high-risk gaps.
   - If any item marked exception, follow Authorization Escape Hatch below.

Authorization Escape Hatch (short-term exception pathway)
- Purpose: allow controlled, auditable, time-boxed exceptions when launch cannot wait and a non-blocking, compensating control is available.
- Who can trigger: release manager in coordination with on-call SRE and security on-call.
- Minimum required artifacts to open an exception:
   1) Exception request form (link to template below) populated in Jira with tag SECURITY_EXCEPTION.
   2) Compensating controls checklist (e.g., IP allow-listing, read-only mode, rate limits enforced, temporary audit-level ramp).
   3) Evidence snapshot: current RBAC state, exact diff from expected, sample audit log showing the missing field, SIEM receipt attempt.
   4) Timebox: maximum 72 hours. Longer requires exec approval and security director sign-off.
- Approval flow: release manager -> security on-call -> infra on-call -> optional TPM escalation. Approvals recorded as comments in Jira and mirrored to archived evidence bundle.
- Post-mortem: required within 72 hours. Root cause, remediation timeline, and policy change assigned.

Exception triage matrix (quick reference):
- Risk = Likelihood x Impact (high/med/low)
- Examples:
   - Missing model_variant_tag in audit logs: medium risk (hard to map model lineage) -> temporary mitigations: enforce model-tag header, enable verbose logging, exception allowed with security approval.
   - RBAC wildcard introduced in role assignment PR: high risk -> block release unless short-term policy applied to single resource and additional monitoring deployed.
   - SIEM export transient failure: low->med risk -> if export can be replayed and TTL respected, exception allowed.

Audit log schema mapping notes (implementation hints):
- Use structured JSON events (not freeform text) with strict types. Keep schema stable across minor releases; add optional fields with explicit versions.
- Reserve a metadata object for provenance: { source_pipeline_version, collector_checksum, collection_window } - this helps automated evidence assembly.
- map of field -> SIEM field: actor_id -> user.id, actor_role -> user.role, request_id -> event.request_id, timestamp_utc -> @timestamp, model_variant_tag -> tags.model_variant
- Ensure redaction hooks documented: PII fields must be redacted before SIEM export; leave token hashes and request ids intact.

Evidence automation runbook (ops steps):
1) Kick off evidence-collector with release tag and time window.
2) Collector fetches: RBAC config from auth service, audit logs from log store (filtered), SIEM ingestion receipts, canary metrics, PR/commit list.
3) Collector produces: zip archive with README, JSON manifest, and short play-by-play of checks executed.
4) Upload to secure bucket and attach to Jira release ticket.

Sign-off template (copy into PR comment or Jira):
- Release tag: <release-tag>
- RBAC v2 verification: OK / EXCEPTION (details)
- Audit schema validated: OK / EXCEPTION (details)
- SIEM export verified: OK / EXCEPTION (details)
- Evidence bundle: link
- Security reviewer: name + timestamp
- Release manager: name + timestamp

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we want the collector to also capture a full request replay for one failing case? Pros: easier debugging. Cons: may contain PII, heavier retention. Need product opinion (ticket JIRA-SEC-941).
- Automate RBAC smoke-tests as a pre-merge CI job? Current friction: role matrix lives in two places. Action: consolidation RFC.
- Can we add a SIEM ingestion ack endpoint to speed evidence generation? Patch in progress PR-312 linked above.

Related tickets and threads:
- JIRA-SEC-934: RBAC v2 rollout schedule and change window
- Slack: #sec-release-approvals thread 2025-05-28 (see pinned messages)
- PR: ops/pull/312 - evidence collector improvements (upload receipts)

Notes and meta: this is intentionally concise. Keep this as the lightweight operational checklist; long-form policy belongs on Confluence. Use this doc during last-mile ops coordination. If you find yourself pasting the same exception justification 3 times, add that rationale to the template above.

-- Asha (security)
